metadata.title: ORCHID-Parity: DFT-vs-experiment formation-enthalpy benchmark
metadata.description:
ORCHID-Parity: DFT-vs-experiment formation-enthalpy benchmark: formation enthalpies of binary compounds read from published papers (ORCHID-Values) paired with the lowest-energy Materials Project and OQMD entries at exactly the same composition, as separate sources that are never averaged. Part of the ORCHID data release v2026.10. Short name in the paper: Parity.

Status. Version 1, machine-extracted: values were read by language-model readers constrained to quote their source and checked automatically, and the release was then audited on the printed pages by adversarial audits, an independent second review of fit-facing records and a preliminary human review of a frozen sample. Flags such as accepted and ESPEI-ready record screening results, not certification; known issues are listed in the release notes.

What

  • 7,646 literature-record x DFT-source points (3,679 Materials Project, 3,967 OQMD) from 4,067 matched records covering 965 compounds; residual = DFT - literature, kJ/mol-atom (1 eV/atom = 96.485 kJ/mol-atom).
  • Default subset (experimental, accepted, signed, not magnitude-suspect): MAE 9.6 kJ/mol-atom over 1,070 Materials Project pairs (Spearman 0.86) and 8.3 over 1,107 OQMD pairs (Spearman 0.91); statistics by chemistry, method and evidence class, exclusions counted by reason. The full pair table includes multiple evidence classes; the reported DFT–experiment statistics use the documented screened experimental subset.
  • Cross-check against Kim et al. 2017 experimental formation enthalpies: 160 formulas in common, MAE 3.76 kJ/mol-atom, sign agreement 99%, 19 formulas differing by more than 10 kJ/mol-atom listed with record ids. The Kim comparison describes its recorded build and must be regenerated against the frozen release before its numerical results are used as current validation.
  • Files: literature/dft_parity.json (rules, statistics, points, records, papers), literature/kim2017_crosscheck.json|.md, Parquet dft_parity.

How

Formulas are parsed from printed phase labels; reduced compositions (4-decimal mole fractions) are matched to non-deprecated DFT entries; large residuals were classified deterministically (per-formula values labelled per atom converted, unsigned magnitudes flagged and excluded, the rest flagged and kept; literature/QUALITY_FIXES.md).

Limitations

  • Literature values are machine-extracted (Version 1); each point keeps its quote and page so it can be checked.
  • Binary compounds only; values whose per-atom basis is not stated are excluded.
  • These discrepancies reflect DFT error together with residual uncertainty in extraction, composition, temperature, provenance and reference state, and are not independent measurements of DFT error alone.
  • MP and OQMD energies use different references and are not comparable with each other.

Licence

ORCHID's data are released under CC BY 4.0, as are the SGTE (B. Hallstedt, Calphad 89 (2025) 102833), Materials Project and OQMD data from which they are derived; attributions and statements of changes are in NOTICE.md, the licence of each folder in LICENSES.md (both in the bundle). The quotations from papers that accompany values are short excerpts kept for verification; they remain under the publishers' copyright and are not relicensed. Source papers, page images and full texts are not redistributed. The Kim et al. 2017 values used in the cross-check come from the Figshare deposit 10.6084/m9.figshare.7289723 under the MIT licence (notice in NOTICE.md).

The stated licence covers the ORCHID-produced content in this deposit; upstream data and software retain their documented terms and attribution requirements, and no publisher pages, handbook drawings or restricted TDB source files are included.

Files: one zip (orchid-dft-benchmark-v2026.10.zip) holding the files at their repository paths, a MANIFEST.sha256, the README, CHANGELOG and licence files. Its file list with sizes and SHA-256 is zenodo/dft-benchmark.files.json in the data repository.

Software and data citations

These credits describe the ORCHID project and its examples. Cite the papers and software used in your analysis, together with the ORCHID release and original source of each observation. The list does not imply that every dataset was generated with every package. Preserve the versions and commit hashes recorded by each example; a repository link is not a reproducibility pin. Materials Project and OQMD energies retain separate references.

  • pycalphad: Thermodynamic calculations and phase equilibria. R. Otis and Z.-K. Liu (2017), pycalphad: CALPHAD-based Computational Thermodynamics in Python (10.5334/jors.140). Repository.
  • ESPEI: Thermodynamic parameter fitting and uncertainty quantification. B. Bocklund et al. (2019), ESPEI for efficient thermodynamic database development, modification, and uncertainty quantification: application to Cu–Mg (10.1557/mrc.2019.59). Repository.
  • PhaseForge: MLIP-informed CALPHAD construction in the examples. S. Zhu, D. Sarıtürk, and R. Arróyave (2025), Machine learning potentials for alloys: a detailed workflow to predict phase diagrams and benchmark accuracy (10.1038/s41524-025-01814-z). Repository; archived software.
  • PhaseForge+: Construction and experimental tuning of CALPHAD models in the examples; repository name PhaseForgePlus. C. Kunselman, S. Zhu, D. Sarıtürk, and R. Arróyave (2025), Construction and Tuning of CALPHAD Models Using Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials and Experimental Data: A Case Study of the Pt–W System (10.1007/s11669-025-01222-2). Repository; archived software.
  • Materials Project: DFT structures and energies; repository link is the API client, not the database itself. A. Jain et al. (2013), Commentary: The Materials Project: A materials genome approach to accelerating materials innovation (10.1063/1.4812323). Repository; data resource.
  • OQMD: DFT structures and energies; qmpy is the supporting software. J. E. Saal et al. (2013), Materials Design and Discovery with High-Throughput Density Functional Theory: The Open Quantum Materials Database (OQMD) (10.1007/s11837-013-0755-4); S. Kirklin et al. (2015), The Open Quantum Materials Database (OQMD): assessing the accuracy of DFT formation energies (10.1038/npjcompumats.2015.10). Repository; data resource.
